hood_landmark.Gastown: the whistling Gastown Steam Clock on Water Street
hood_landmark.Yaletown: converted-warehouse patios along the False Creek seawall and the Roundhouse
hood_landmark.Kitsilano: Kits Beach with its huge saltwater pool and mountain views
hood_landmark.West End: English Bay Beach at the doorstep of Stanley Park
hood_landmark.Mount Pleasant: Main Street's giant murals from the Vancouver Mural Festival

avoid.reason: Downtown Eastside (Hastings St) — visible open drug use and homelessness; otherwise very safe

hood_desc: Gastown is Vancouver's historic cobblestone quarter with Victorian buildings, the famous steam clock, trendy restaurants and boutiques, great for visitors and young professionals who want walkable heritage charm and nightlife.

Yaletown is a polished former warehouse district of converted brick lofts, waterfront seawall and marina, upscale patios and design shops, suits affluent professionals and foodies who want a sleek downtown-adjacent scene.
Kitsilano is a laid-back beachside neighborhood with Kits Beach, health-focused cafes and yoga studios, and boutique shopping along West 4th, ideal for active, outdoorsy people and young families.

The West End is a dense, diverse and highly walkable residential area between Stanley Park and English Bay, home to the LGBTQ-friendly Davie Village, perfect for those wanting an urban beach lifestyle without a car.
Mount Pleasant is the artsy, hip heart of the city with Main Street's indie shops, craft breweries, murals and coffee roasters, a magnet for creatives, students and trend-conscious young locals.

water.note: Tap water is safe and comes from protected mountain watersheds.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone at any fare gate or bus reader - no setup needed - or buy a Compass Card (C$6 refundable deposit) from station vending machines and London Drugs stores. Adult fares run about C$3.35-6.60 (~US$2.45-4.85) depending on zones; buses are one zone flat. The same tap covers SkyTrain, buses and the SeaBus to North Vancouver.
transit.hours: SkyTrain runs about 5am-1:30am (shorter Sundays); NightBus routes cover main corridors after closing.

transit.m: Canada Line SkyTrain to downtown (~26 min)

landmarks: Stanley Park
A massive urban rainforest park with seawall views, totem poles, and skyline backdrops that make it endlessly photogenic.
Capilano Suspension Bridge
A historic swaying footbridge 70m above a forested canyon, offering dramatic treetop and gorge photos.
Canada Place
The sail-roofed cruise terminal and convention centre on the waterfront is Vancouver's most recognizable architectural silhouette.
Vancouver Lookout
A revolving-view observation tower atop Harbour Centre giving 360-degree panoramas of the city and mountains.
Granville Island Public Market
A colorful waterfront market of food stalls, artisans, and boats beneath the Granville Street Bridge, beloved for street photography.
Science World at TELUS World of Science
The distinctive silver geodesic dome on False Creek is one of Vancouver's most photographed structures, especially at sunset.
Grouse Mountain
A short gondola ride up gives sweeping views of the city, ocean, and North Shore mountains, popular for skyline shots.
Lions Gate Bridge
The elegant suspension bridge spanning Burrard Inlet, framed beautifully by Stanley Park and the mountains beyond.
Gastown Steam Clock
A whimsical steam-powered clock in the cobblestoned historic district, a classic close-up photo stop.
Queen Elizabeth Park
Vancouver's highest point offers manicured gardens, a quarry garden, and skyline views ideal for sweeping cityscape shots.

train.note: The Cascades to Seattle (continuing to Portland/Eugene) is a true international train - it leaves from Pacific Central Station with US border formalities before boarding, so arrive early with your passport. VIA Rail's Canadian to Jasper and Toronto departs from the same station.

bus.note: Cross-border coaches pick up downtown (Waterfront/Canada Place area for Quick Coach; Pacific Central for FlixBus) and clear US customs at the border - passport required. Ebus and Rider Express handle domestic routes within BC and beyond.

ferry.note: No international ferries from Vancouver - the Victoria-Seattle Clipper leaves from Victoria, not Vancouver. Domestic BC Ferries (https://www.bcferries.com/) sail to Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands from Tsawwassen and Horseshoe Bay terminals, both ~40 min from downtown.

half.name: Squamish

half.name: Deep Cove
half.blurb: Tranquil seaside village on a fjord, perfect for kayaking, gentle hikes and waterfront strolls.

half.name: Steveston
half.blurb: Historic fishing village with a working harbour, fresh seafood and a boardwalk along the river.

full.name: Victoria
full.blurb: Elegant harbourfront capital with gardens, heritage architecture and a scenic ferry crossing through the islands.
